mode: Bounded measured implementation. Three pages, one deferred dependency each, every number below read out of a real headless Chrome over S3-R11's fixture world.

instruments.runner: assets/tests/_s4r4-deferred-read-runner.js - five scenarios (shape, reentry, failure, stale, invalidation) over the real shipped page code.
instruments.world: assets/tests/_s3r11-interaction-runner.js, extended this round with the six tables these three pages read. S4-R1 recorded factory-stock and carrier-rate-card with useful:0 because the world did not carry them; request counts were still true, but no scenario could reach a row.
instruments.listeners: S4-R2's listener probe, imported rather than copied, so a disagreement about drift would mean the application changed and not the instrument.

what_is_authoritative: Request counts and the TABLES behind them. A count is a property of control flow and holds at any server speed.
READ ROUNDS, derived from sent/settled marks - with a bounded read pool the cost a user waits through is how many reads were paid for one after another.
DOM outcomes: what the first useful screen contains, whether a refusal is visible, whether the primary table survived it.
Deferred-dependency state transitions, read from KM.deferredRead.state().
what_is_not_observable: MILLISECONDS. Under --virtual-time-budget Chrome freezes the clock inside a task; S4-R1 measured this and S4-R3 repeated it. No figure in this file is a duration.
Whether the deferred read feels faster to a person. What IS measured is the two things §11 asks for: the first useful UI renders without the deferred data, and the secondary load does not block it.
instrument_corrections_this_round: LISTENER DRIFT IS A MARGINAL RATE. A first reading took the census before a page's FIRST mount and reported +89 and +65 for two pages S4-R2 had sealed at 0. Those listeners are one-time registrations that a live page is entitled to - document-level handlers, and elements inside a section that is hidden rather than removed. The baseline now starts after one mount and one unmount, which is the statistic S4-R2 sealed, and all three pages read 0.

THE FAILURE SCENARIO LIFTS ITS REFUSALS BEFORE RETRY. A scoped read rejects its whole batch on the first refusal, so arming four tables and then pressing Retry re-refused the two the first attempt never reached - and reported the page as failing to recover from a network that was in fact still down.
TWO ERROR-BOX SELECTORS MATCHED STATIC HOSTS rather than errors, so a healthy page counted a refusal it had not had.
THE FACTORY SNAPSHOT RENDERS DIVS, NOT ROWS. S4-R1's census asked for `tr` and recorded useful:0 for a table that was full; the correct selector is .fixed-row and the table has 40.

campaign-risk.label: Promotion Risk Tracker
campaign-risk.firstUsefulUi: the Country <select>, built from the distinct countries of ACTIVE marketplace_skus
campaign-risk.whyDeferrable: CampaignRiskState.country starts empty and nothing restores it, so crScopeReady() is false on every cold entry. getSkuMasterData() and _crScopedPromotions() both return [] without a scope, and renderRiskKPIs() prints three neutral zeros by design. The page cannot show a row or a non-zero KPI on first entry whatever these four tables contain.
campaign-risk.postWrite: NONE. This page has no DB write: promotions are a localStorage overlay (savePromotionRecords). Nothing it can do changes campaigns, campaign_sku_lines, marketplaces or sku_details.

firstConsumerCost.note: One READ of one dependency. The request count is the number of TABLES in that dependency, because a scoped read asks per table - it is not four dependencies.

doubleFire.note: The interaction fired twice with no wait between, from a freshly invalidated state: two callers reaching ensure() while one read is in flight. Equal to firstConsumerCost is the contract.

factory-stock.label: Factory Inventory
factory-stock.firstConsumer: the Movement Log tab is opened (switchFactoryTab)
factory-stock.whyDeferrable: The Movement Log panel ships with style="display:none". Its only data consumer, _getDbFactoryMovementData(), is reached from _populateFactoryMovFilters() - which ran at mount from _initFactoryMovementLog - and from renderFactoryMovementTable(), which is search-gated. The mount was filling dropdowns in a hidden panel.
factory-stock.postWrite: INVALIDATE, and re-read when held. An inventory adjustment appends to factory_stock_movements. _fsAfterWrite re-reads the movements table when the tab is open (a visible log that lacked the row just written would be a lie) and invalidates it when it is not (the next tab open pays for one read).

carrier-rate-card.label: Carrier Rate Card
carrier-rate-card.firstUsefulUi: the faceted filter bar; the table is empty by design until Search
carrier-rate-card.whyDeferrable: The single consumer of carrier_lead_times is _crcLeadTimeMap(), called only from _crcRender(), called only from search(). _crcInit() populates the facets and prints "Set filters and click Search". The facets need the rate cards (options) and carriers (labels) - not the lead times.
carrier-rate-card.postWrite: NONE REQUIRED. The only write on this page imports carrier_rate_cards. The page states the separation itself: Lead Time and transit_days are maintained in carrier_lead_times and are never stored on rate cards, so a rate-card import cannot make the lead-time model stale.
